sections.title: Prospectus Summary
text: Source Agriventures is an early stage farmland-focused real asset and sustainable agriculture company that seeks to generate long-term value by combining high-quality agricultural real estate with regenerative farming, clean-energy development and strategic Agricultural Technology (“AgTech”) investments. Source Agriventures has a limited operating history: We currently own one farming property located in Illinois and plan to acquire more, as part of a broader operational strategy that will include a number of business verticals. Our business is built on the belief that farmland is a scarce, essential and increasingly valuable resource, and that the next generation of agricultural land ownership will be driven not only by crop production, but also by improved land stewardship, diversified revenue streams and the integration of modern technology that are combined to increase return on investment.

A part of our strategy is the acquisition and long-term ownership of productive farmland in the Midwest and the Sun Belt regions of the United States, which is then leased to experienced operators through structured arrangements designed to produce stable and recurring rental income. Our goal is to partner with tenant farmers and encourage the adoption of regenerative practices such as reduced tillage, optimized fertilizer use and cover cropping. We seek to enhance soil health and long-term productivity while positioning properties that we acquire to generate additional value through the sale of carbon credits. These practices support both environmental resilience and the emerging economics of carbon sequestration, which we believe represent a significant opportunity for forward-looking farmland owners. To date, our leasing activity has been limited to leasing a single piece of land, and we have not begun any carbon sequestration or sale activities.

sections.title: Risk Factors
text: Investing in our Common Stock involves a high degree of risk. Before investing in our Common Stock, you should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information in this prospectus, including our financial statements and the related notes. In addition, we may face additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us, or which as of the date of this Registration Statement we might not consider significant, which may adversely affect our business. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected. In such case, the trading price of our Common Stock could decline due to any of these risks or uncertainties, and you may lose part or all of your investment.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, we reported a net loss of $177,528, bringing our accumulated deficit to $326,519. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, we reported a net loss of $114,040, bringing our accumulated deficit to $440,559.

We have minimal revenues and expect significant increases in costs and expenses as we invest in expanding our acquisition of farmland and investments in AgTech businesses. Even if we are successful in increasing revenues from our leasing and partnerships, we may be unable to achieve positive cash flow or profitability for a number of reasons, including but not limited to, increased land costs, increases in our general and administrative expenses, and a reduction in our rental income due to competitive or other factors. An inability to generate positive cash flow and profitability until we reach a sufficient level of sales with positive gross margins that cover operating expenses, or an inability to raise additional capital on reasonable terms, will adversely affect our viability as an operating business.

sections.title: Prior Performance Summary
text: The Company has not previously sponsored or managed any public or private real estate investment programs, real estate investment trusts, or limited partnerships. Accordingly, the Company has no predecessor programs or affiliated investment programs whose historical results may be presented as prior performance information or relied upon as indicative of future results. Prospective investors should evaluate the Company based on its current business plan, operating history, financial condition and the risks described elsewhere in this prospectus.

Investors should not assume that the Company’s limited historical operations or current assets will be indicative of future performance. The Company remains in an early stage of development, has a concentrated asset base, and its future performance will depend on its ability to acquire and operate additional farmland investments and execute its growth strategy. Please see “Risk Factors” for a discussion of the risks associated with investing in the Company.

The Company was incorporated in Nevada in May 2023 and changed its name from Source Agriculture Corp. to Source Agriventures Inc. in August 2025 to reflect its focus on agricultural real assets and related investment opportunities.

As of June 30, 2026, the Company has completed one farmland acquisition, consisting of approximately 158 acres of farmland located in Macon County, Illinois, which was acquired on March 21, 2024 for approximately $2.75 million. The Illinois Farm is leased to a tenant under a multi-year lease arrangement. The Company has also entered into a renewable energy development lease relating to the Illinois Farm and has made minority investments in three early-stage AgTech companies.

text: Market sales of shares of our Common Stock after this offering, or the availability of such shares for sale, may adversely affect the market price of our Common Stock. Sales of substantial amounts of our Common Stock, or the perception that such sales could occur, could also impair our ability to raise capital through future offerings of equity securities. Upon completion of this offering and expiration of the applicable lock-up periods, all shares sold in this offering will be freely tradable without restriction under the Securities Act, except for shares purchased by our affiliates, as that term is defined in Rule 144 under the Securities Act. Shares of our Common Stock that are not being registered in this offering will be eligible for public resale from time to time in compliance with Rule 144 or other applicable exemptions.

Our Company, officers, directors and substantially all of our company’s stockholders holding at least ten percent (10%) of the outstanding Common Stock have agreed, subject to certain exceptions, to a 6-month “lock-up” period after the closing of the IPO with respect to the Common Stock that they beneficially own, including the issuance of shares upon the exercise of convertible securities and options that are currently outstanding or which may be issued. The Underwriter has no present intention to waive or shorten the lock-up or standstill period; however, the terms of the lock-up agreements may be waived at its discretion. sections.title: Notes to Financial Statements
text: Source Agriventures Inc. (formerly “Source Agriculture Corp.”) (the “Company”), incorporated under the Nevada Business Corporation Act on May 30, 2023, is an agriculture land acquisition and agtech development company specializing in the agriculture and agri-tech sectors. The Company collaborates with companies that are developing sustainable solutions to address the challenges of modern agriculture. The Company is committed to supporting technologies that improve the efficiency, productivity, and environmental footprint of farming worldwide. The head office of the Company is located at 540 5th Avenue SW, Suite 1410, Calgary, Alberta T2P 0M2, and the registered and records office of the Company is located at 3064 Silver Sage DR STE 150, Carson City, Nevada, United States, 89701.

In August 2025, the Company changed its name from Source Agriculture Corp. to Source Agriventures Inc. to reflect the Company’s evolution into a modern agriculture leader investing in renewable energy projects, revolutionary agtech, and the future of sustainable farming.
The financial statements were approved and authorized for issuance on February 27, 2026 by the board of directors of the Company.

The financial statements of the Company have been prepared in accordance with rules and regulations of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) and generally accepted accounting principles in the United States (“U.S. GAAP”) and are expressed in U.S. dollars.

This summary of significant accounting policies of the Company is presented to assist in understanding the Company’s financial statements. The financial statements and notes are representations of the Company’s management who are responsible for their integrity and objectivity. These accounting policies conform to accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America and have been consistently applied in the preparation of the financial statements.

summary: We have not reached profitability and currently have negative operating cash flows.
Our ability to operate effectively could be impaired if we fail to retain or recruit key personnel.
We have a very limited operating history and have not demonstrated an ability to acquire or profitably operate a farmland-focused real asset platform at scale.
Tariffs, trade restrictions and other governmental actions could adversely affect the profitability of our tenants and, indirectly, the value and returns of our farmland investments.
Global economic conditions, including elevated levels of inflation and supply chain disruptions, could materially and adversely affect our and our tenants’ operations.
We may not be able to identify and acquire suitable farmland properties on acceptable terms.

We may acquire farmland that is subject to title defects, boundary disputes, easements, encroachments, liens or other encumbrances, which could adversely affect our ownership rights, development plans or property values.

Zoning laws, land-use restrictions and permitting requirements may prevent us from developing renewable energy projects, installing data centers, or pursuing other higher-value uses of farmland that we acquire.
Our farmland leasing strategy exposes us to tenant-related risks, including default, non-renewal, declining crop yields and changes in commodity prices.
We may be unable to renew leases or re-lease properties as leases expire.
Farmland values and rental rates are subject to fluctuations outside of our control.
We may from time to time be subject to claims of infringement of third-party intellectual property rights, which could harm our business.
The success of our carbon credit strategy depends on the adoption of regenerative farming practices by our tenant farmers, which we do not control.
Carbon credits carry significant risk due to uncertainty.
Renewable energy development and AI data center development are each highly regulated and subject to zoning, environmental and permitting risks that may prevent or delay project development.
We may not successfully develop, install or monetize renewable energy projects on farmland that we acquire.
Investments in early-stage AgTech businesses are risky, speculative and may result in a total loss of capital.

Any significant limitation or failure of our technology systems, or of our third-party vendors’ technology systems, or any security breach of our information and cyber security infrastructure, software applications, technology or other systems that are critical to our operations could interrupt or damage our operations and result in material financial loss, regulatory violations, reputational harm
We face significant competition across each of our proposed business verticals, which could adversely affect our ability to execute our strategy and achieve profitability.

Our operations are subject to extensive agricultural, land use and environmental regulation, which could increase costs, limit permissible uses of properties we may acquire and materially adversely affect our business.

Our renewable energy, carbon credit and potential data center initiatives are subject to complex and uncertain regulatory frameworks that could delay or prevent projects and reduce anticipated economic benefits.
Our business is subject to seasonality and cyclical conditions inherent in the agricultural industry, which may cause variability in our results of operations.
We may not have adequate insurance coverage to protect against all potential losses, which could adversely affect our financial condition.

Our strategy depends on maintaining strong relationships with third-parties such as farmers, renewable energy developers, engineering firms, and carbon credit partners, and disruptions to these relationships may materially impact our business.
We are an “emerging growth company,” and we cannot be certain if the reduced reporting requirements applicable to emerging growth companies will make our Common Stock less attractive to investors.
Our strategy of developing data centers on properties that may also be used for agricultural purposes could create operational challenges and increase costs.

Although we do not believe that the Company is, or will be, considered an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940 (the “Investment Company Act”), if the Company were nevertheless deemed to be an investment company, it could be required to institute burdensome compliance requirements and its activities could be restricted.

We have acquired only one farmland property to date and held our current property for only a limited period of time and thus you will not have the opportunity to evaluate our future acquisitions before we make them, which makes your investment more speculative.
Our management team has limited direct experience operating farmland properties, which may increase the risks associated with an investment in our Company.
Conflicts of interest may arise due to our directors and officers serving, or serving in the future, as directors and officers of other companies.
Our operations and business may be significantly impacted by adverse weather conditions, climate change and other environmental risks.
Environmental contamination on properties we acquire could require significant remediation costs and reduce our ability to use or monetize those properties.

Farmland properties that we acquire may be affected by water scarcity, water-rights restrictions or changes in water availability caused by drought, regulation, climate change, or the downstream impacts of AI data centers.
You will experience immediate and substantial dilution as a result of this offering and may experience additional dilution in the future.
Management will have broad discretion as to the use of the proceeds from this offering, and we may not use the proceeds effectively.

We may need to raise additional funds to support our business operations or to finance future acquisitions, including through the issuance of equity or debt securities, which could have a material adverse effect on our ability to grow our business.
We are not subject to any limit on the amount of leverage we may incur, which could increase the risks associated with an investment in us.
We will incur increased costs as a result of operating as a U.S. public reporting company, and our management is required to devote substantial time to new compliance initiatives.

We have no operating experience as a publicly traded company in the United States and any failure to maintain effective internal controls over financial reporting could adversely affect our business and the market price of our Common Stock.

Our inability to comply with the continued exchange listing requirements could result in our Common Stock being delisted, which could affect the market price and liquidity of our Common Stock and reduce our ability to raise capital.

notes.title: CASH AND CASH EQUIVALENTS
text: There were no cash equivalents held as at December 31, 2025. As at December 31, 2024, the Company had cash equivalents of $1,900,000 invested in a short-term deposit earning interest at a rate of 4.35%, with a maturity date of January 19, 2025.

notes.title: LAND, AT COST
text: On March 21, 2024, the Company purchased agricultural land (“Sinkosky Farm”) situated in Macon County, Illinois, USA for a total cost of $2,746,551 (includes commission and directly attributable acquisition cost of $14,159).

There were no indicators of impairment identified as of and during the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024. The land continues to be carried at cost in accordance with ASC 360, Property, Plant and Equipment.

notes.title: INVESTMENTS
text: (i) On November 14, 2024, the Company entered into a preferred stock purchase agreement with SwineTech Inc., a private company and the creator of PigFlow, a transformative workforce and swine management platform. In accordance with ASC 321, the Company has elected to account for the investment at cost minus impairment until its fair value becomes readily determinable.

(ii) On November 20, 2024, the Company entered into a Simple Agreement for Future Equity (“SAFE”) with Ascribe Bioscience Inc., a private company dedicated to developing sustainable crop protection solutions. During the year ended December 31, 2025, Ascribe Bioscience completed a Series A Preferred Stock financing, which triggered the conversion of the SAFE into Series A Preferred Stock. The financing confirmed the value of the Company’s investment to be $100,000 and no gain or loss were recorded on conversion. In accordance with ASC 321, the Company has elected to account for the investment at cost minus impairment until its fair value becomes readily determinable.

notes.title: OPERATING LEASE
text: Effective March 1, 2024, the Company entered into an operating lease with a tenant on its Sinkosky Farm. The lease has a three-year term, expiring on February 28, 2027. Base rent amounts to $71,005 per year and is due in advance on or before March 1 each year.

Effective September 6, 2024, the Company entered into an operating lease with a renewable energy company wanting to install wind turbines and wind turbine infrastructure on the Sinkosky Farm. The Company received a signing bonus of $5,560 payable on execution of the lease. During the development period, which ends on September 6, 2031, the Company is entitled to annual rent starting with $2,383 in the first year, escalating annually by approximately 6%, to $3,336 in the 7th year. The agreement includes provisions for additional rent should the tenant elect to install a temporary or permanent meteorological tower. In addition, should the tenant move forward with construction and operation, the Company will be entitled to construction payments and additional annual rent during the operations term.
